title: Veneer seedkit: idempotent Terraform module for Redwood Private EKS control planes
creator: Maya Patterson
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (internal name: veneer-seedkit) to bootstrap and manage Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs. This module should be operatorless (no custom controllers required), idempotent across repeated apply operations, and instrumented with preflight validations, continuous health checks, and an automated canary-safe upgrade path. The module will target both AWS accounts we provision for customers and cross-account KMS configurations required for control plane secrets. Output examples, runbook snippets, and a CLI quickstart will be included in the module README.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys into an empty VPC and produces a healthy EKS control plane with worker nodegroups or node pools as configured (using eksctl or eks module).
Repeated terraform apply on the same state is a no-op (idempotent) with zero destructive diffs unless inputs change explicitly.
Preflight checks run during plan/apply and fail fast if critical invariants are missing (subnets, route tables, service endpoints).
A canary upgrade flow exists: module produces a canary cluster or canary control-plane flag that allows staged API server upgrade, with automated rollback on health regression triggers.
Module exposes CloudWatch (or Datadog) metrics and alerts for control-plane health: API server availability, etcd quorum, control-plane node CPU/memory, kube-controller-manager errors.
KMS keys and encryption config can be provisioned cross-account or accept an existing CMK ARN; secrets are never left unencrypted in state or logs.
Comprehensive README with inputs/outputs, example usage, upgrade runbook, and terraform-integration tests (terragrunt/terratest) included.
Security review checklist completed and signed off by security team (link in comments).
E2E smoke test recorded in CI that validates basic API functionality post-provision and post-upgrade.

design_notes: High-level constraints: module must be usable by both 'Redwood-managed' and 'customer-managed' AWS accounts. We avoid adding cluster controllers to minimize runtime maintenance; instead the module creates IAM roles, EKS control plane resources, nodegroups (optional), config maps for RBAC bootstrap, and optional managed addons (coredns, kube-proxy). The 'veneer' concept is that the module surfaces opinionated defaults (networking, kubelet config, kubeadm-like patches) but allows overrides. We will encode upgrade strategy as a staged apply pattern: 1) create new control-plane revision flag resource, 2) apply worker node rotation, 3) run health gating tests, 4) flip traffic. If gating fails, terraform destroy of the revision resources combined with pre-recorded snapshots will trigger rollback orchestrations. To avoid long-lived secrets in state, we accept CMK ARNs and use data sources + kms_grant resources instead of storing plaintext keys. For metrics we rely on CloudWatch metric filters and push select metrics into Datadog via an existing forwarder lambda. The module will expose a 'health_check_lambda' hook so customers can supply a custom probe if needed.
decisions: Operatorless approach chosen to reduce runtime support burden — no new controllers will be deployed to customer clusters.
Use terraform null_resource + local-exec for preflight checks instead of a separate orchestration service to keep setup simple and auditable.
Canary upgrades implemented as separate revision resources rather than in-place control-plane patching to make rollback deterministic.
Do not store unencrypted bootstrap tokens in state; require customers to supply a secure secret manager or pre-created CMK.
Default addons will be managed addons to reduce divergence from AWS supported lifecycle.
Terratest (Go) will be the primary integration test harness; small shell-based quick smoke tests used in CI for speed.
